intro.en: Every program you run becomes a process. Modern programs also split their work into threads so they can do several things at once, like a browser loading a page while you scroll.
intro.ru: Har chalne wala program ek process ban jata hai. Aaj ke programs apna kaam threads mein bhi baant dete hain taake ek waqt mein kai kaam ho sakein, jaise browser page load karta rahe aur aap scroll karte rahein.

definition.en: A process is a program in execution with its own address space and resources. A thread is the smallest unit of CPU scheduling inside a process; threads of the same process share its memory and open files but each has its own registers, program counter and stack.
definition.ru: Process chalta hua program hai jis ka apna address space aur resources hote hain. Thread process ke andar CPU scheduling ki sab se chhoti unit hai; ek process ke threads us ki memory aur open files share karte hain lekin har thread ke apne registers, program counter aur stack hote hain.

explanation.en: The operating system keeps a Process Control Block (PCB) for every process: process id, state, program counter, CPU registers, memory information and open files. A process moves between states: new, ready (waiting for the CPU), running, waiting/blocked (waiting for I/O) and terminated. Switching the CPU from one process to another is a context switch: the OS saves the old PCB state and loads the new one, which costs time. Creating a process (fork) copies or maps a whole address space, so it is expensive; creating a thread is cheaper because threads share the address space. Threads make programs responsive and let them use several CPU cores, but shared memory means threads must synchronise to avoid race conditions. A crash in one thread can bring down the whole process, while processes are isolated from each other.
explanation.ru: Operating system har process ke liye Process Control Block (PCB) rakhta hai: process id, state, program counter, CPU registers, memory ki maloomat aur open files. Process mukhtalif states se guzarta hai: new, ready (CPU ka intezar), running, waiting/blocked (I/O ka intezar) aur terminated. CPU ko ek process se doosre par le jana context switch kehlata hai: OS purane PCB ki halat save karta hai aur naya load karta hai, jis mein waqt lagta hai. Naya process banana (fork) poora address space copy ya map karta hai, is liye mehenga hai; thread banana sasta hai kyunki threads address space share karte hain. Threads program ko tez jawab dene wala banate hain aur kai CPU cores istemal karne dete hain, lekin shared memory ki wajah se threads ko race conditions se bachne ke liye synchronise karna parta hai. Ek thread crash ho to poora process gir sakta hai, jabke processes ek doosre se alag (isolated) hote hain.

example.en: A web browser can run each tab as a separate process: if one tab crashes, the others keep working (isolation). Inside one tab, separate threads handle the network download, the page rendering and your mouse clicks at the same time (shared memory, cheap switching).
example.ru: Web browser har tab ko alag process ke taur par chala sakta hai: ek tab crash ho to baqi chalte rehte hain (isolation). Ek tab ke andar alag threads ek hi waqt mein network download, page rendering aur mouse clicks sambhalte hain (shared memory, sasti switching).

intro.en: When several processes are ready, the CPU scheduler decides which one runs next. The choice changes how long users wait, so scheduling is one of the most examined OS topics.
intro.ru: Jab kai processes ready hon to CPU scheduler tay karta hai ke agla kaun chalega. Is faisle se users ka intezar badalta hai, is liye scheduling OS ke sab se zyada exam mein aane wale topics mein se hai.

definition.en: CPU scheduling is the policy that selects which ready process gets the CPU next. Common algorithms are First-Come-First-Served (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF), Priority and Round Robin (RR).
definition.ru: CPU scheduling woh policy hai jo tay karti hai ke ready processes mein se agla CPU kis ko mile. Mashhoor algorithms First-Come-First-Served (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF), Priority aur Round Robin (RR) hain.

explanation.en: Key measures: turnaround time = completion time - arrival time; waiting time = turnaround time - burst time; response time = first run - arrival. FCFS runs processes in arrival order; it is simple but a long job in front makes everyone wait (convoy effect). SJF picks the shortest burst next and gives the minimum average waiting time among non-preemptive algorithms, but needs burst lengths in advance and can starve long jobs. SRTF is its preemptive version. Priority scheduling runs the highest priority first; aging (raising the priority of old processes) prevents starvation. Round Robin gives each process a fixed time quantum in turn; it is fair and gives good response time, but a very small quantum causes many context switches and a very large quantum turns it into FCFS. Results are shown with a Gantt chart.
explanation.ru: Ahem paimane: turnaround time = completion time - arrival time; waiting time = turnaround time - burst time; response time = pehli dafa chalna - arrival. FCFS processes ko aane ki tarteeb se chalata hai; saada hai lekin aage lamba kaam ho to sab intezar karte hain (convoy effect). SJF agla sab se chhota burst chunta hai aur non-preemptive algorithms mein sab se kam average waiting time deta hai, lekin bursts pehle se maloom hone chahiye aur lambe kaam bhookay (starve) reh sakte hain. SRTF is ka preemptive version hai. Priority scheduling sab se zyada priority wala pehle chalati hai; aging (purane processes ki priority barhana) starvation rokta hai. Round Robin har process ko bari bari ek muqarrar time quantum deta hai; yeh insaaf wala hai aur jaldi response deta hai, lekin bohat chhota quantum bohat se context switches karwata hai aur bohat bara quantum ise FCFS bana deta hai. Natije Gantt chart se dikhaye jate hain.

example.en: Processes (arrival, burst): P1 (0, 5), P2 (1, 3), P3 (2, 1). FCFS order P1, P2, P3: completion 5, 8, 9; turnaround 5, 7, 7; waiting 0, 4, 6; average waiting = 10/3 = 3.33. Non-preemptive SJF: P1 runs 0-5 (only one ready), then P3 (burst 1) 5-6, then P2 6-9; waiting 0, 5, 3; average = 8/3 = 2.67. Run the OS scheduling simulator to see the Gantt charts and try Round Robin.
example.ru: Processes (arrival, burst): P1 (0, 5), P2 (1, 3), P3 (2, 1). FCFS tarteeb P1, P2, P3: completion 5, 8, 9; turnaround 5, 7, 7; waiting 0, 4, 6; average waiting = 10/3 = 3.33. Non-preemptive SJF: P1 0-5 (sirf yahi ready tha), phir P3 (burst 1) 5-6, phir P2 6-9; waiting 0, 5, 3; average = 8/3 = 2.67. Gantt charts dekhne aur Round Robin try karne ke liye OS scheduling simulator chalayein.

intro.en: When threads or processes share data, the order in which they run can corrupt it. Synchronization tools make sure shared data stays correct.
intro.ru: Jab threads ya processes data share karte hain to un ke chalne ki tarteeb data ko kharab kar sakti hai. Synchronization ke tools yaqeeni banate hain ke shared data durust rahe.

definition.en: A race condition occurs when the result depends on the timing of concurrent accesses to shared data. The code that accesses shared data is the critical section; synchronization (locks, semaphores, monitors) ensures that at most one process executes its critical section at a time.
definition.ru: Race condition tab hoti hai jab natija is baat par munhasir ho ke shared data ko concurrent tor par kis waqt access kiya gaya. Shared data ko access karne wala code critical section hai; synchronization (locks, semaphores, monitors) yaqeeni banati hai ke ek waqt mein zyada se zyada ek process apne critical section mein ho.

explanation.en: A correct solution to the critical-section problem needs mutual exclusion (only one process inside), progress (a free critical section must be given to a waiting process) and bounded waiting (no process waits forever). A semaphore is an integer S with two atomic operations: wait(S) (also P or down) decrements S and blocks if it becomes negative; signal(S) (V or up) increments S and wakes a waiting process. A binary semaphore (0/1) works like a mutex lock; a counting semaphore counts available resources. The producer-consumer (bounded buffer) problem uses three semaphores: mutex = 1 for buffer access, empty = n for free slots and full = 0 for filled slots. Wrong ordering of wait calls can cause deadlock.
explanation.ru: Critical-section masle ke sahi hal ko teen cheezein chahiye: mutual exclusion (andar sirf ek process), progress (khali critical section intezar karne wale process ko mile) aur bounded waiting (koi process hamesha intezar na kare). Semaphore ek integer S hai jis ke do atomic operations hain: wait(S) (P ya down) S ko kam karta hai aur manfi ho jaye to block karta hai; signal(S) (V ya up) S ko barhata hai aur intezar karne wale process ko jagata hai. Binary semaphore (0/1) mutex lock ki tarah hai; counting semaphore dastiyab resources ginta hai. Producer-consumer (bounded buffer) masla teen semaphores istemal karta hai: mutex = 1 buffer ke liye, empty = n khali jagahon ke liye aur full = 0 bhari jagahon ke liye. wait calls ki ghalat tarteeb deadlock karwa sakti hai.

example.en: Two threads each run counter = counter + 1 on a shared counter of 5. Each loads 5, adds 1 and stores 6, so the result is 6 instead of 7: a race condition. Wrapping the update in wait(mutex) ... signal(mutex) with mutex = 1 makes the second thread wait, so the result is 7.
example.ru: Do threads shared counter (value 5) par counter = counter + 1 chalate hain. Dono 5 load karte hain, 1 jama karte hain aur 6 store karte hain, natija 7 ki jagah 6: race condition. Update ko mutex = 1 ke saath wait(mutex) ... signal(mutex) mein band karne se doosra thread intezar karta hai aur natija 7 aata hai.

subject: Operating Systems

intro.en: Deadlock is a classic operating-system problem in which programs wait for each other forever, so none of them can continue.
intro.ru: Deadlock operating system ka classic masla hai jis mein programs hamesha ek doosre ka intezar karte rehte hain aur koi aage nahi barh pata.

definition.en: A deadlock is a state in which each process in a set holds at least one resource and waits for a resource held by another process in the same set, so none of them can proceed.
definition.ru: Deadlock aisi halat hai jis mein ek group ka har process kam az kam ek resource pakre hota hai aur usi group ke kisi doosre process ke resource ka intezar karta hai, is liye koi bhi aage nahi barh sakta.

explanation.en: A deadlock can only happen when four (Coffman) conditions hold at the same time: mutual exclusion (a resource can be used by one process at a time), hold and wait (a process holds resources while waiting for more), no preemption (resources cannot be taken away), and circular wait (a cycle of processes each waiting for the next). Handling strategies: prevention breaks one condition (e.g. request all resources at once, or order resources and always request them in that order); avoidance grants requests only if the system stays in a safe state (Banker's algorithm); detection builds a wait-for / resource-allocation graph and looks for a cycle, then recovers by terminating a process or preempting resources; or the system ignores the problem (the 'ostrich' approach used by many desktop OSs).
explanation.ru: Deadlock sirf tab hota hai jab chaar (Coffman) conditions ek saath poori hon: mutual exclusion (resource ek waqt mein ek process istemal kare), hold and wait (process resources pakre hue mazeed ka intezar kare), no preemption (resources cheene nahi ja sakte), aur circular wait (processes ka daira jis mein har ek agle ka intezar kare). Hal ke tareeqe: prevention ek condition tor deta hai (maslan saare resources ek saath maangna, ya resources ko tarteeb de kar hamesha usi tarteeb mein maangna); avoidance sirf tab request deta hai jab system safe state mein rahe (Banker's algorithm); detection wait-for / resource-allocation graph bana kar cycle dhoondta hai, phir process khatam kar ke ya resources cheen kar recover karta hai; ya system masle ko nazar andaz karta hai ('ostrich' tareeqa, kai desktop OS yahi karte hain).

example.en: Process P1 holds the printer and requests the scanner. Process P2 holds the scanner and requests the printer. Both wait forever: mutual exclusion (one user per device), hold and wait (each holds one), no preemption (the OS will not take the printer away), circular wait (P1 -> P2 -> P1). If both processes always request the printer before the scanner (resource ordering), circular wait is impossible and the deadlock cannot occur.
example.ru: Process P1 printer pakre hue scanner maangta hai. Process P2 scanner pakre hue printer maangta hai. Dono hamesha intezar karte rehte hain: mutual exclusion (ek device ka ek user), hold and wait (har ek ne ek pakra hai), no preemption (OS printer nahi cheenta), circular wait (P1 -> P2 -> P1). Agar dono hamesha pehle printer phir scanner maangein (resource ordering), to circular wait mumkin nahi aur deadlock nahi hoga.

intro.en: Paging lets the operating system place a program's memory in any free frames of RAM, and virtual memory lets programs be larger than RAM by keeping some pages on disk.
intro.ru: Paging OS ko program ki memory RAM ke kisi bhi khali frame mein rakhne deti hai, aur virtual memory programs ko RAM se bara hone deti hai kyunki kuch pages disk par rakhe jate hain.

definition.en: Paging divides logical memory into fixed-size pages and physical memory into frames of the same size; a page table maps each page number to a frame number. Virtual memory loads pages only when they are needed (demand paging) and triggers a page fault when a page is not in memory.
definition.ru: Paging logical memory ko barabar size ke pages aur physical memory ko usi size ke frames mein baantti hai; page table har page number ko frame number se jorta hai. Virtual memory pages sirf zaroorat par load karti hai (demand paging) aur jab page memory mein na ho to page fault hota hai.

explanation.en: A logical address is split into a page number p (high bits) and an offset d (low bits). With page size 2^n bytes, the offset has n bits. The page table gives the frame number f, and the physical address is f x page size + d. Paging removes external fragmentation, but the last page of a process may be partly empty (internal fragmentation). Every memory access now needs an extra page-table lookup, so a small cache called the TLB stores recent translations. Effective access time with a TLB = hit ratio x (TLB time + memory time) + miss ratio x (TLB time + 2 x memory time). On a page fault the OS finds the page on disk, loads it into a free frame (or evicts one with a page replacement algorithm), updates the page table and restarts the instruction.
explanation.ru: Logical address page number p (upar ke bits) aur offset d (neeche ke bits) mein toot-ta hai. Page size 2^n bytes ho to offset ke n bits hote hain. Page table frame number f deti hai, aur physical address = f x page size + d. Paging external fragmentation khatam karti hai, lekin process ka aakhri page aadha khali reh sakta hai (internal fragmentation). Ab har memory access ko page table ka ek izafi lookup chahiye, is liye TLB naam ka chhota cache haal ki translations rakhta hai. TLB ke saath effective access time = hit ratio x (TLB time + memory time) + miss ratio x (TLB time + 2 x memory time). Page fault par OS disk se page dhoondta hai, use khali frame mein load karta hai (ya page replacement algorithm se kisi ko nikalta hai), page table update karta hai aur instruction dobara chalata hai.

example.en: Page size 1 KB (1024 bytes, offset 10 bits). Logical address 2500: page = 2500 // 1024 = 2, offset = 2500 - 2048 = 452. If the page table maps page 2 to frame 5, the physical address = 5 x 1024 + 452 = 5572.
example.ru: Page size 1 KB (1024 bytes, offset 10 bits). Logical address 2500: page = 2500 // 1024 = 2, offset = 2500 - 2048 = 452. Agar page table page 2 ko frame 5 se jore to physical address = 5 x 1024 + 452 = 5572.

intro.en: When RAM is full and a page fault occurs, the OS must choose a page to throw out. A good choice means fewer slow disk reads.
intro.ru: Jab RAM bhari ho aur page fault ho to OS ko koi page nikalna parta hai. Acha intikhab ka matlab kam dheemi disk reads.

definition.en: A page replacement algorithm chooses the victim page to evict on a page fault when no frame is free. Classic algorithms are FIFO (oldest page), LRU (least recently used page) and Optimal (page used farthest in the future).
definition.ru: Page replacement algorithm page fault par, jab koi frame khali na ho, nikalne wala (victim) page chunta hai. Classic algorithms FIFO (sab se purana page), LRU (sab se kam haal mein istemal hua page) aur Optimal (jo page mustaqbil mein sab se der se istemal hoga) hain.

explanation.en: Algorithms are compared by counting page faults on a reference string for a given number of frames. FIFO is simple but suffers from Belady's anomaly: adding frames can increase faults. Optimal (OPT) gives the minimum possible faults but needs future knowledge, so it is only a benchmark. LRU approximates OPT by looking at the past; it is a stack algorithm and never shows Belady's anomaly, but exact LRU needs hardware support (counters or a stack), so real systems use approximations such as the clock (second-chance) algorithm. If processes have too few frames they fault constantly and spend more time paging than running: thrashing.
explanation.ru: Algorithms ka muqabla kisi reference string par diye gaye frames ke saath page faults gin kar hota hai. FIFO saada hai lekin Belady's anomaly ka shikaar hai: frames barhane se faults barh sakte hain. Optimal (OPT) kam se kam mumkin faults deta hai lekin mustaqbil ka ilm chahiye, is liye sirf muqable ka paimana hai. LRU maazi dekh kar OPT ke qareeb aata hai; yeh stack algorithm hai aur is mein Belady's anomaly kabhi nahi hoti, lekin bilkul sahi LRU ko hardware ki madad (counters ya stack) chahiye, is liye asal systems clock (second-chance) jaise approximations istemal karte hain. Agar processes ko bohat kam frames milein to woh lagatar fault karte hain aur chalne se zyada paging mein waqt lagate hain: thrashing.

example.en: Reference string 7, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4 with 3 frames. FIFO: 7, 0, 1 fault (3); 2 replaces 7 (4); 0 hit; 3 replaces 0 (5); 0 replaces 1 (6); 4 replaces 2 (7) - 7 faults. LRU: 7, 0, 1 (3); 2 replaces 7 (4); 0 hit; 3 replaces 1 (5); 0 hit; 4 replaces 2 (6) - 6 faults. Try the page replacement simulator to step through it.
example.ru: Reference string 7, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4, 3 frames. FIFO: 7, 0, 1 fault (3); 2 ne 7 ki jagah li (4); 0 hit; 3 ne 0 ki jagah li (5); 0 ne 1 ki (6); 4 ne 2 ki (7) - 7 faults. LRU: 7, 0, 1 (3); 2 ne 7 ki jagah li (4); 0 hit; 3 ne 1 ki (5); 0 hit; 4 ne 2 ki (6) - 6 faults. Step by step dekhne ke liye page replacement simulator chalayein.
